title: Close a roll-end mailer box: lock both ends by their tabs, then shut and tuck the lid; its walls start folded up
instruction: The box's front and back walls are already folded up: lock both roll ends with every tab in its hole, then shut the lid with its tuck inside the front wall.
context: Hand packers (O*NET 53-7064.00, Core: 'Assemble, line, and pad cartons, crates, and containers, using hand tools'; 559,820 US jobs) and shipping clerks (43-5071.00; 816,870) pack goods, much of it in die-cut mailers that close without tape (FEFCO 0427, roll end, tuck front). The box starts part-erected, after Packlane's step 3: front and back walls folded up, their dust flaps folded in. The robot does every fold after that: it locks both roll ends ('snap each side panel into the holes in the bottom of the box, continuing the same motion'), then shuts the lid and tucks it in. A panel pushed short leaves its tabs on the base, and a tuck pushed in square catches on the wall's edge. Each end wall springs back unless one hand holds it (3 N) while the other rolls its inner panel 180 degrees and presses it down blind until two 2.5 cm tabs drop into 6 x 30 mm holes; the free 0.45 kg box slides under every push. Nearest board tasks fold carton flaps flat; none locks rolled ends by tabs.
setup: Station: two YAM arms with parallel grippers, bases 61 cm apart at the near edge of a 120 x 90 cm wood table, 75 cm high. Positions in cm from the midpoint between the arm bases: x forward, y to the robot's left; heights above the table top. Box: a FEFCO 0427 mailer (one piece, roll ends, tuck front, no glue) in B-flute corrugated board 3.2 mm thick, outside 13 3/8 x 12 3/8 x 6 1/4 in (34.0 x 31.4 x 15.9 cm), 0.45 kg: the outside size, board and mass of a 12 x 12 x 6 in tab-locking mailer (Uline S-16934). A rolled end is 17.5 mm thick, half of Uline's outside less inside length. The die-line is a FEFCO 0427 template at that size: base; front and back walls, each with a 14 x 14 cm dust flap at each end; at each end an outer panel, 31.4 x 15.9 cm, joined over a double crease to its inner panel, 30.5 x 15.2 cm, with two 2.5 cm tabs on its free edge 8 cm each side of the middle; four 6 x 30 mm holes for them in the base, 1.6 cm inside each end's crease; the lid, hinged on the back wall's top, 30.7 cm to its tuck's crease, and the tuck, 28 x 4.5 cm, its free corners rounded to 15 mm. Start state, the same every trial: the box part-erected. Its front and back walls and their four dust flaps start folded, as after step 3 of Packlane's five-step guide; the robot does every fold after that: it locks both roll ends, then shuts the lid and tucks it in. The base lies flat on the table, free (nothing holds it; friction about 0.4: Park et al. 2019 give 0.38 static for board on board), its middle at (34, 0), the ends to the robot's left (crease at y 17) and right (y -17), the front wall toward the robot. The front and back walls stand folded up with their dust flaps folded in across the ends (in a real trial the tester folds them up and sets the flaps in by hand before each trial, as after Packlane's step 3, and nothing holds them but the folds until the rolled ends trap the flaps). Each end's outer panel leans out at 80 +/- 5 degrees above the table, where its crease springs it, its inner panel unrolled beyond its top. The lid stands straight up in line with the back wall (its crease not yet folded), the tuck in line with the lid. Both grippers start at the arms' ready pose, 26 cm above the table at (32, 30.5) and (32, -30.5). In simulation (settings, not measurements): holding an end wall upright takes 3 N at its top edge; an inner panel rolled flat inside pushes back with 0.2 N at its free edge; a tab pressed back 3 mm bears on the base with 0.45 N; shut, the lid pushes open with 0.5 N at its front edge until its tuck is in, and a tuck bearing on the front wall's inside holds it against up to 2 N lifting that edge; folded 90 degrees, the tuck springs back with 0.35 N at its edge against 0.27 N of crease friction, so curled past square and let go it springs back onto the wall. The box stays free and slides and turns under the pushes; that is part of the task. Reset: unhook the tabs, roll the panels back out, fold the lid and tuck back up. Replace the box after 10 trials, or once an end wall no longer rests at 80 +/- 5 degrees. A real trial uses S-16934 as bought (Uline, bundle of 25, 4.34 USD each; one box per 10 trials), with a ruler, a square and a protractor; its own tabs, holes and tuck stand in for the modelled ones.
scoring: Measured at the end with photos from the front and above, a ruler and a square; each tab checked from underneath. An end is rolled when its inner panel is folded past 100 degrees, its free edge inside the box and below the wall's top; down when the panel is within 10 degrees of flat against the wall and its edge within 1 cm of the base; locked when both its tabs are in their holes (tip at least 2 mm down into the base, inside the hole's outline; real trial: seen from underneath), the inner panel within 2 degrees of flat (real trial: the wall's top flat, 'not slanted or peaked', Packlane's own check), the wall within 5 degrees of upright (real trial: square) and both dust flaps within 10 degrees of folded in. The lid is shut within 5 degrees of flat (real trial: its front edge within 2.5 cm of the front wall's top by ruler), and tucked when its tuck is folded down 60 degrees or more with its face on the front wall's inside (its face on it: a gap of 0.6 mm at most), at least 2 cm below the top (real trial: tuck not visible from above, lid stays down when let go). Tiers: each end 0.4 (0.1 rolled, 0.2 down, 0.3 one tab in, 0.4 locked); the lid 0.2, counted only with both ends locked (0.1 shut, 0.2 tucked). All three done: 0.95; 1.0 also needs both grippers' fingers at least 3 cm from the closed box's outside and no point of the box moving more than 1 mm over that last 1 s. The score is the state at the end, held 1 s: a step undone before the end loses its tier. Score 0, and it stays 0, if the box leaves the bench (its middle past the bench edge or below it) or the board is damaged: a tab torn or bent past 45 degrees, a new fold or tear away from the creases, a dent deeper than 2 mm, or a dust flap forced out past 30 degrees. Sliding, turning or tipping the box costs nothing by itself. Possible scores: 0, 0.1 to 0.8 in steps of 0.1, 0.9, 0.95, 1.0.
fidelity: Whole box at Uline S-16934's outside size. Front and back walls start folded up, rigid with the base; dust flaps sprung shut (real: spring out). Panels are rigid, weightless plates on sprung hinges (creases are settings); no cardboard skew; no lid side flaps. Each double crease is one hinge; a tab latches 2 mm in its hole; the tuck latches the lid. Simulation scores only bench-leave and dust-flap (past 30 deg) damage; tab, fold, dent need a real trial. The demo reads the scorer's state.
reset_notes: Nothing is random (object_jitter=0). Between real trials unhook the tabs, roll the inner panels back out, fold the lid and tuck back up in line with the back wall; replace the box after 10 trials or once an end wall no longer rests at 80 +/- 5 degrees.
